tag: the closure vocabulary becomes free text, so a rate over it is invisible to every projection
why: L2(f). The vocabulary is closed for the same reason --by refuses anything that is not a round id: a rate computed over prose is invisible to every projection, which is exactly how the register came to record five closures of three different kinds identically.

tag: a closure does not record why it closed
why: L2(a) — FU-314 itself. Without the field, retrospection cannot tell a round that BUILT from a round that MEASURED, and both the item rate and the row rate read a measurement close as if it were a build.

tag: the kind is stored without its meaning, so a reader must know the vocabulary
why: L2(a). A four-word token in a register is a category a later reader guesses at; the meaning travels with it so the row explains itself without the CLI that wrote it.

tag: a closure with no reason passes silently
old:
said.append("closed" + (f" as {args.because}" if args.because else
                                    " with NO --because, so retrospection cannot tell what kind of "
                                    "closure this was"))
why: L2(b). Omitting --because is ALLOWED - refusing would make every historical closure unrepeatable - but it must never be invisible, or the field will simply go unused and the defect returns with the mechanism in place.

tag: a row records both the reachability check and that the check cannot be recovered
why: L2(e). They are alternatives: recording HOW reachability was established and that it CANNOT BE RECOVERED is a contradiction, and whichever a later reader believed would be a coin toss. The Owner's ruling of 2026-10-03 turns on which rows are auditable.

tag: the reachability check is accepted and never stored
why: L2(c), and it is the worst shape available here: the CLI would accept --check, print success, and record nothing - so a round would believe it had satisfied P2.4's second leg while leaving the register exactly as empty as before.

tag: an unrecoverable check is silently absent instead of named
why: L2(d), and the Owner's ruling says it in as many words: every row whose check cannot be recovered is marked UNAUDITED BY NAME rather than passed over. An absent field reads as a row nobody looked at.

tag: retrospection counts the unrecorded closures as builds
why: L3, and it is the subtlest defect in this round. Every row closed before W561 carries no kind; attributing them to 'built' would INVENT the very distinction the field exists to stop inventing, and it would do so in the direction that flatters the programme - 200-odd closures all reading as work done.

tag: the mix is not reported at all, so the faculty still cannot see kind
why: L3. FU-314's own words: '_retrospect then reports the mix'. A field written into the register that no faculty reads is the stored-and-not-rendered shape this method exists to catch.

tag: a ruling is missing from the Owner's block
old: · -n 6 IS WHAT A COMMIT IS TRUSTED TO
why: L4. The rulings are constitution and a later round may not widen, soften or reinterpret them - which requires that they are all actually there to be read. The mutation softens a ruling into a preference, which is the exact failure mode the constitution clause names.

tag: the questions decided WITHOUT the Owner are not recorded, so the filtering cannot be audited
old: WHAT WAS DECIDED WITHOUT ASKING, recorded so the filtering is auditable:
why: L4. Twelve questions were surfaced and five were put to the Owner; the other seven were decided. Recording WHICH is what lets the Owner check that the filtering was reasonable - without it, the five look like the whole set and the judgement behind the other seven is invisible.
